text:
maria_support: FYI customer reported a sudden change in responses after yesterday's rollout. They say short prompts now get an extra lead-in sentence that wasn't there before. Pasting their repro and token counts.

maria_support: CUSTOMER SNIP:
> user prompt: "Summarize the following product note."
> response (before rollout): "In short: ..."
> response (after rollout): "Note: The assistant may summarize differently... In short: ...

maria_support: they attached tokenized lengths: before=12 tokens, after=18 tokens (extra preface tokens). Customer: "this started after the deploy yesterday at ~03:15 UTC"

emma_custsuccess: looping in @kevin_ml and @jasper_engineer — customer marks P1, production traffic impacted :warning:

kevin_ml: initial hunch: we changed chat preamble trimming in tokenizer v2.2; small whitespace/newline handling can shift token boundaries and trigger a different assistant behavior (safety preface or system-preamble duplication). Can you paste the raw request body + model id?

maria_support: here's the curl they sent (redacted api key):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-3b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following product note."}]}'
```

jasper_engineer: I can repro locally when I run the same payload against redwood-chat-3b@v2026-03-16 with tokenizer v2.2. The difference is tiny: if system.content has a trailing newline or an extra leading space, token boundaries change and the model emits a brief preface. Repro steps:
```bash
# reproduce
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer('v2.1').encode('You are a helpful assistant.'))"
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer('v2.2').encode('You are a helpful assistant.\n'))"
# v2.2 produces an extra leading token in many model vocabularies
```
jasper_engineer: note: it's not just stripping — we now normalize trailing whitespace which shifts how the system + user messages concatenate in the runtime. That seems to surface safety-preface logic in the front-end model prompt.

kevin_ml: also check routing: some tenants were routed to the new variant during the rollout; if their system prompt concatenation order differs slightly we can amplify the effect. @ops_bot can you confirm which variant served acme between 03:00-03:30 UTC?

ops_bot: queried logs for tenant "acme-corp" -> served by pool dedicated-us-west-2-a, model variant redwood-chat-3b@v2026-03-16 from 03:12:10 to 03:45:02 UTC (approx).

emma_custsuccess: customer asks for immediate mitigation — can we give a config they can set to opt back to previous behavior, or else rollback?

jasper_engineer: quick mitigation: runtime supports a compatibility header we didn't document yet. Temporary header: `X-Redwood-Tokenizer: legacy` forces old tokenization on the request path. I can push a flag to route for that tenant and add an e2e test. Longer term we should either revert the trimming behavior or add an explicit opt-in. I'll open PR and a rollback ticket.

kevin_ml: create incident/rollback plan if more customers report. Logging ticket created: IN-2026-042.

maria_support: sending the header to the customer and asking them to confirm whether responses match old behavior when they include it. Will update thread with their confirmation. Thanks team :pray:

jasper_engineer: I'll also add unit tests covering system/user concatenation edge cases and preserve exact whitespace inside system messages. Patch draft incoming.

kevin_ml: good. After customer confirms, coordinate a canary rollback or hotfix.

maria_support: noted, will follow up.
